messages:
taylor: Customer Priya (acme-inc) reports intermittent 403s and occasional huge latency (~10s) on production since this morning. Happens when hitting /v1/generate. They saw a billing-related banner in the UI before the errors. Need request IDs, curl repro, and a debug bundle. Can anyone triage? :eyes:
priya: seeing 403 with body 'billing_required' and sometimes 502 when it times out. first observed at 2026-03-16T09:03:15Z. example request id: req-0a1b2c3d4e. stacktrace attached in their ticket.
ben: can you paste the full response headers and the request headers (no API key)? also need the trace id if available (x-rw-trace-id). 403+billing usually points to the billing guard but let's not assume.
taylor: pasted the redacted response from priya below:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
x-rw-req-id: req-0a1b2c3d4e
x-rw-trace-id: trace-77a9
{"error":"billing_required","message":"Payment method declined"}
```

ben: ok got req id. Priya, can you run this curl from the UI host and paste output? it should help repro: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-3.1-quant","input":"hello"}' \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
```

priya: running now — FYI we're on model pin: `model=gpt-redwood-3.1-quant` via our account-level pin.

anya: two things to check while we wait: 1) whether canary routing is enabled for that model variant (we rolled a canary last night), 2) if fallback policy is misconfigured to return 403 instead of falling back to stable. Ben, can you check routing logs for req-0a1b2c3d4e?

ben: pulled routing logs for req-0a1b2c3d4e: it hit router node r-4, was routed to canary pool cp-12, then backend returned 403 from billing-guard service. Trace shows attempt to fallback but the fallback policy returned 403 because the customer account is flagged. Snip of logs:
```
[2026-03-16T09:03:15Z] req=req-0a1b2c3d4e router=r-4 pool=cp-12 -> backend=gpt-redwood-3.1-quant-canary status=403 billing_guard=declined fallback_attempt=1 fallback_result=403
```

anya: interesting — so the backend itself flagged billing_required, fallback didn't bypass billing check (as expected). That suggests either a real billing issue or our billing service returned false positive due to recent billing sync job.

priya: customer insists their payment is valid — they updated card yesterday. They can share billing invoice id if needed.

ben: next steps for repro bundle: Priya, please run our debug bundle collector on one of the failing requests (this will capture headers, req/resp, and traces). From the host that hit the API run:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REPLACE_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/debug/collect?req=req-0a1b2c3d4e" -o debug-acme-190123.tar.gz
```
Then upload to the ticket or share link. That gives us full traces.

ops-bot: deploy 190123 started by ci-cd (canary rollout for gpt-redwood-3.1-quant).
deploy-bot: canary swap completed on 2026-03-16T02:12:43Z to cp-12.

taylor: while we wait for the debug bundle, can someone confirm model pin behavior: if account pins model X and canary is serving X-canary, should router redirect to canary? My understanding: account-level pin pins model family, not variant, so canaries still apply unless customer sets strict-version pin.

anya: correct. pin granularity: family vs exact artifact. account-level family pin will allow variant routing; strict pin uses full artifact hash which blocks canaries. Priya, do you know which pin type acme-inc is using?

priya: they told us 'pin to gpt-redwood-3.1-quant' via Console UI (looks like family pin).

anya: that explains canary hit. For repro: we should try to reproduce both with family pin (current setup) and with strict pin to see if fallback path changes. Ben, can you simulate a strict pin request with a header override?

ben: done — using `X-RW-Pin: gpt-redwood-3.1-quant@sha256:deadbeef` header simulated strict pin; that request bypassed canary and routed to stable pool sp-3 and returned 200. So stable works. 

priya: looks like customer's family pin caused canary routing which hit billing guard. They want to stay on this model though. What's remediation?

anya: options: 1) ask Billing to re-validate the account (most likely), 2) temporarily strict-pin customer to stable artifact to avoid canary until billing sync resolves, 3) change router fallback policy to prefer stable instead of returning 403 on billing_guard (not ideal).

ben: for immediate mitigation I can set the account to strict pin (manual override) for acme-inc; it'll avoid canary. Priya, want me to do that?

priya: yes please, that'll buy us time. Also we uploaded debug bundle: link https://uploads.redwood.ai/debug/debug-acme-190123.tar.gz (contains traces & headers).

ben: strict pin applied for acme-inc at 2026-03-16T10:05:00Z. Monitoring for further 403s.

ops-bot: alert suppressed for acme-inc 403 after strict pin applied.

anya: I'll loop in billing to re-run the sync and check for false positives. Ben — can you also run a traffic replay for the failing requests against stable and canary to collect latency profiles?

ben: scheduled a small replay for req-0a1b2c4..7 against both pools, will attach results to ticket. initial numbers show canary latency 1.8s median but had 10s tail when it hit billing-guard retry path.

priya: thanks team — customer confirmed errors stopped after strict pin. They want us to follow up with a root cause.

Taylor: summary for ticket: collected req ids (req-0a1b2c3d4e), debug bundle uploaded, confirmed canary routing due to family pin, strict pin mitigated immediate failures, billing team to investigate false-positive decline. I'll keep ticket updated. :white_check_mark:
